What do you guys think about the venus project?

It's a cult, and its ideals are Stalinist.

Here is economist Robert P. Murphy on the Venus Project's economic illiteracy: https://mises.org/library/venus-needs-some-austrians

Here is a critical look at the Venus Project and its founder, Jacque Fresco: http://www.thenewamerican.com/world-news/north-america/item/10634-zeitgeist-and-the-venus-project

And this one is from liberal blogger George Waye: https://outofthegdwaye.wordpress.com/2014/02/24/the-venus-project-everything-wrong-with-utopian-fantasy-in-108-simple-questions/

  1. The Venus Project is a cult. Every person who knows anything about the Venus Project knows that the ideas, mission, and credit belong to one person. You can’t navigate a page on their website or magazine without seeing the name Jacque Fresco. Even when he is spectacularly wrong, his acolytes can’t muster more than tepid deference. The only argument you can make against this is that a cult traditionally has a charismatic leader, and Jacques Fresco has all the personality of Joe Leiberman on Unisom.

  2. The Venus Project is naive scientism. Science is not going to solve all the worlds problems, it’s just not. It’s not going to make human dynamics less complicated and it’s not a panacea to every imaginable problem. Sometimes problems require more than just an invention or technology. Even if Jacque Fresco could invent a machine to bring Nikola Tesla back to life- it still wouldn’t solve all our problems. Well, most of them. But not all.

  3. Jacque Fresco knows how to design a building. Jacque Fresco does not know how to design a society or an economy. He certainly doesn’t know anything about sociology, psychology or economics. He is a futurist- but unless technology can make humans behave like algorithms- he is just blowing smoke.

I think there are some things of value of the Venus project. The biggest being the Global resource management system. We are one planet, and we need a way to distribute goods/resources around this planet that does not lead to hierarchies between peoples. This is a way to get around that. That being said there is differently some culty vibes in the Venus project and TZM for that matter, but their are some nuggets in there.

I like the ideals of TZM but don't personally think Fresco's Project is an answer to all the worlds problems since building different societies is usually a never ending process rather than a finite vision that's completely planned out by one person, or group, from start to finish.

It's just straight up foolish and hopelessly naive. Basically a less interesting version of the Zeitgeist Movement. They make all the high minded claims about how wise and great things will be run but they don't have a single accountability process even discussed. What happens when a corrupt leader gets into power? There's nothing, it's all run on the assumption that people can be trained to think a certain way and that doing that will mean that everyone isn't corrupt.

Minted Pea Soup

Ingredients

3 tbsp olive oil
1 medium-sized yellow onion, chopped
4 cups vegetable broth, divided
6 cups shelled frozen peas
1/2 cup fresh mint leaves, gently packed (about a bunch), or more to taste
salt
freshly ground pepper

Directions

  1. Pour olive oil in a large heavy pot, over medium heat. Add onion and cook until softened and transparent.

  2. Add 3 cups of broth.

  3. When it has reached a boil, add peas and cook for about 4-5minutes, or until tender.

  4. Remove from heat and add the mint leaves.

  5. Purée soup using an immersion blender, adding more broth to reach a smooth yet thick consistency. Taste, adding salt and pepper accordingly.

This soup can be eaten cold or warm, and cubed ham can be added (to the latter version), as well as heavy cream.
